Layout options

Source: R/layout-options.R
layout_size.Rd

Options that apply to the whole figure.

Usage

layout_size(layout, width = NULL, height = NULL)

layout_spacing(layout, inner = NULL, outer = NULL)

layout_tags(layout, tags = "A", fontsize = 10, fontface = "bold")

layout_title(layout, title, fontsize = 12, fontface = "bold")

Arguments

layout

A layout, ggplot or grob.

width, height

Figure size in mm. NULL leaves it unchanged, NA unsets it.

inner

Gap between plots in mm. One value for both directions, or c(horizontal, vertical). NULL leaves it unchanged, NA returns to the plot margins (also per direction, e.g. c(NA, 5)).

outer

Margin around the whole figure in mm (default 0). NULL leaves it unchanged, NA resets it.

tags

"A", "a", "1", "I", "i", or a character vector of labels.

fontsize, fontface

Text style.

title

Title text.

Value

A layout.

Details

  • layout_size() sets the figure size in mm, e.g. a journal column width (Nature: 89 mm single column, 183 mm double column). Free panels absorb the extra space; if there are none, it becomes slack placed according to the containers' alignment.

  • layout_spacing() sets the gaps between neighbouring plots in mm, measured between their outer boxes (axis labels, legends and tags included). It replaces the plots' own plot.margin, so gaps are even when plots use different themes. Without it, the gaps come from the plot margins. outer adds a margin around the whole figure. Note that axis labels can stick out past their panel (e.g. the last tick label); ggplot2 normally relies on the plot margin for that space. With small gaps, such labels may overlap neighbouring plots, and at the figure's edge they can be cut off; use a small outer margin (1-2 mm) then.

  • layout_tags() adds panel tags. Tags are aligned at the top of their row, even when plots in that row have different heights. To let several plots share one tag, use tag_group().

  • layout_title() adds a title above the figure.

Examples

p1 <- dummy(name = "p1", color = "#0072B2")
p2 <- dummy(name = "p2", color = "#D55E00", height = 45)
p3 <- dummy(name = "p3", color = "#009E73", width = NA)

new_row(p1, p2) |>
  new_row(p3) |>
  layout_tags("A") |>
  layout_title("My figure") |>
  layout_size(width = 120)


new_row(p1, p2) |>
  new_row(p3) |>
  layout_spacing(inner = 2, outer = 5)


new_row(p1, p2) |>
  new_row(p3) |>
  layout_spacing(inner = c(2, 6))
